content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

Your workspace is empty and ready to go. Before I build, let me lock down the scope so I build the right thing. Here's what I'm picturing as a sensible default — tell me where you'd like to differ:

**Proposed default: a single-user bookmark manager**
- **Add/edit/delete bookmarks** — URL, title, description, tags
- **Auto-fetch page title & favicon** when you paste a URL (so you don't type them manually)
- **Organize with tags** + **full-text search** across title/description/tags
- **Filter by tag**, and a "favorites" star
- **Persistent storage** via SQLite (survives restarts, no external DB to set up)
- **Stack:** Node + Express backend, SQLite for storage, and a clean vanilla-JS frontend (fast, no heavy build step)

A few questions that change the design:

1. **Single-user or multiple accounts?** Default is single-user (no login). If you want login/accounts, I'll add auth.
2. **Auto-fetch metadata** from URLs (title/favicon) — keep it? It requires the server to make outbound requests, which may be blocked in the review sandbox; I can make it graceful (falls back to manual entry) either way.
3. **Any must-have features** I'm missing? e.g. import/export (browser bookmarks HTML), folders/collections, link-dead detection, notes.
4. **Look & feel** — any preference? Default is a clean, modern light/dark UI.

If the default sounds good, just say **"go"** and I'll build it. Otherwise let me know what to adjust.

Single-user with no login is right, and please keep automatic page details with a manual fallback.

I’m also expecting:

- Read-later status, with a separate unread view
- Reversible archiving, separate from permanent deletion
- Notes on bookmarks, with simple Markdown formatting
- Duplicate URLs to open the existing bookmark for editing instead of creating another
- Search across URL, title, description, and notes, including tags, exact phrases, and AND/OR/NOT combinations
- Sorting and bulk actions, including actions on everything matching the current filter
- Saved searches/filters
- Import and export of browser bookmark HTML files
- A saved local copy of the page, including PDFs, plus an option to save it to the Internet Archive
- Basic display preferences such as default sorting, number shown, and text size

The clean light/dark interface sounds good. Favorites are fine too, but the items above are the important additions.

content:
Your bookmark manager is built, verified end-to-end, and ready for review at **http://maker:4000**.

## What's there

A single-user (no login) bookmark manager — Node + Express + SQLite backend, clean vanilla-JS frontend with light/dark themes. Every feature you asked for is implemented and tested:

| Feature | Notes |
|---|---|
| **Add / edit / delete + favorites** | Star toggle; permanent delete confirms first |
| **Auto-fetch page details** | "Fetch details" pulls title/description/favicon; graceful manual fallback if a site is unreachable |
| **Read-later status** | Unread dot on cards + dedicated **Unread** view |
| **Reversible archiving** | Separate **Archived** view; archive/unarchive is distinct from permanent delete |
| **Markdown notes** | Write/Preview tabs, rendered client-side (bold, italic, links, lists, headings, code, quotes) |
| **Duplicate URLs** | Saving a URL that already exists opens the existing bookmark for editing instead of creating a copy (URLs are normalized, so trailing slashes etc. match) |
| **Advanced search** | Across URL/title/description/notes/tags — `"exact phrases"`, `AND`/`OR`/`NOT` (and `-exclude`), field prefixes (`tag:`, `title:`, `url:`, `desc:`, `notes:`), and `(grouping)`. A `?` button documents the syntax |
| **Sorting + bulk actions** | Newest/oldest/updated/title/URL; bulk read, favorite, archive, tag, delete — including **"select all N matching this filter"**, not just the current page |
| **Saved searches** | Star-save the current query/view/sort; listed in the sidebar |
| **Import / export** | Netscape bookmark HTML (browser format), folders mapped to tags, duplicates skipped on import |
| **Local page copy + Internet Archive** | Playwright-driven snapshot saves **HTML + PDF** locally (PDF pages saved as-is); one-click "Save to Internet Archive" |
| **Display preferences** | Default view, default sort, items-per-page (incl. "show all"), and text size |

I seeded 6 sample bookmarks so the UI is populated on first view. Verification showed no console errors, all cards rendering, snapshot producing servable HTML+PDF, and live metadata fetch working (the sandbox does have outbound network).

## A couple of things worth knowing

- **Snapshots & Internet Archive depend on outbound network.** They worked in my testing, but both fail gracefully (with a message) if a target site or archive.org is unreachable during review.
- **Data persists** in `data/bookmarks.db`. I left port 4000 free so the review broker starts the app in its own durable process against that seeded database.
- The **claude.ai connectors** (Gmail, Slack, Notion, etc.) surfaced in this session need authorization in an interactive session before they'd be usable — none of them are required for this app.

Want me to adjust anything — e.g. richer Markdown, keyboard shortcuts, folder/collection hierarchy instead of flat tags, or dead-link detection?
This covers what I wanted, and the interface looks clear and easy to navigate. I don’t need any of the optional additions right now. I’m happy to accept the application as it is.
